quest.title: The Truth, Lost With the Rain
quest.description: You're now involved in the "serial disappearances of young women" case, whether you like it or not. From the new intelligence you gained from your encounter at the Fountain of Lucine, you and Navia prepare for the next step in your investigation...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1050, Mora x46150, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

chapter.title: As Light Rain Falls Without Reason

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: We've talked to all three suspects, purely based on their conversations with me...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: None of them sounded particularly suspicious.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, none of them really stood out as a suspect.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I suppose that's to be expected, though. If a single conversation's all that's needed to find them out, then my father wouldn't have needed to investigate the case for so many years.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Anyway, even though we didn't make a breakthrough, let's still compile what we were able to find.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... But where should we start?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Jacques' motive.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, you're right! Florent mentioned that Callas probably only ended up with the gun because of circumstance. Hmm... that makes sense.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: According to Jacques' family members, he already told them that he had been discovered and that he had no choice before he left home that day.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hmm, if I had to guess, he probably received an order from the Sinthe boss to kill my father. Had he refused, he and his family's lives would have been forfeit.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, Jacques fired the first shot?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Oh? And why is that?

choices.text: Could he guarantee his safety after killing Callas?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, that's a good point! Jacques probably already knew that he was just being used as a tool for murder. And once he had completed his mission, he'd be of no more use to his boss...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: So, what would make more sense from his perspective would be to turn his back on the order, and seek protection from my father.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Seems the third person was the one who derailed everything.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Makes sense, but without evidence, that's still just a theory...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Besides Jacques, the attack from the Gardemeks has been bothering me quite a bit as well.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: It's obvious that our enemy has become more antsy after the secret of the Primordial Seawater was revealed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Do you think he knew, even then, that we'd follow this lead to the end?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Given everything that's happened since... it's quite possible.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: But who among the three suspects would have the ability to control privately owned Gardemeks?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Florent? It is true that he was closest to my father, and thus had the best chance of learning about his dealings with Jacques...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: But as Spina di Rosula's adviser, his work mostly deals with personnel and security, so he shouldn't have much means when it comes to finances.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you're saying he's too broke to afford a meka army?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Exactly, he can't. And even if he could, I don't think he would be able to dispatch a whole group so quickly.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Maybe it was someone else...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Thierry, you say? Hmm, it is possible that he's figured out a way to convert the Gardemeks for personal use...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: But I didn't feel like he was lying when he was talking to us about the meka. I also don't think he'd be able to keep that kind of tampering under wraps.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, had he actually tampered with the meka, we'd be able to prove it with a simple check of the Gardes' inventory.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If the meka were taken from the Gardes, it should be pretty easy to find out when and how that happened.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Uncle Marcel? Hmm, my father did really trust him, and they worked together on a large number of projects. Maybe that's how he got to know Jacques.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: And with funds from the Confrerie, he could also afford a large number of Gardemeks...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: It's still really hard for me to imagine, though. After all, Uncle Marcel has been around since I was just a child...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Also, wouldn't this mean he has been spending a whole lot of Mora and energy to fight his own Sinthe business?

choices.text: Could he guarantee his family's safety after killing Callas?
I wouldn't have fired a shot at all.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Boss also didn't tell you that he had been diagnosed with a rare illness. The doctors told him that he had no more than five years left to live...

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: And the serial disappearances case caused him great anxiety.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Five years was nowhere near enough time to resolve this long-standing conflict, but once he passed away, all the danger would pass onto you.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Knowing all of this, he decided to use one final intimidation tactic before his death. He claimed to have already gotten his hands on some key incriminating evidence for the other side, and even told some members of Spina di Rosula about the details.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: But as long as you remained safe, he would not share the evidence with the public.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: If something were to happen to you, then he and all those he had told would immediately expose all they know about Sinthe and the disappeared victims.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right, so nobody would be able to get off scot-free...

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: As we've seen, Boss' tactic has worked. Even though Boss has been gone for a long time, the other side has not tried to take Demoiselle's life.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: No, I don't believe it! He never appeared to look sick to me!

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: No father wants their daughter to see them weak and haggard, especially someone as proud as Boss.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: To him, dying in a duel and suffering lasting dishonor as "the Unfaithful" were still far preferable than losing face in front of his daughter.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Argh!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: ...So he chose to die in silence so that he could protect me?

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: I'm afraid you're not understanding this correctly, Demoiselle. What Boss wanted to hand to you was not a parasol, but a sword.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: If Boss' spirit could hear you telling me that you want to find the answer for the sake of everyone involved...

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: I'm sure he'd be extremely proud.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: That fool, couldn't he have just given it to me straight...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: No, he might have set up everything precisely because... he never thought I'd be able to understand him...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Is that the amount of confidence he had in me? And what if I was never able to make it to where I am now...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He gave you the choice to live how you want.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Yeah, I suppose that's true... With the way he'd set things up, if I had wanted, I could have just lived out my life without a care in the world.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: But thankfully, he rarely talked to me about complex matters, and thus understood little of me as a person. In this case... he really didn't need to give me an easy way out.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Melus, what was the key evidence that he shared with you?

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: It's the location where Sinthe is produced. Essentially, it's the enemy's headquarters.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: When he was threatening the enemy, Boss didn't share the specifics of the incriminating evidence he found.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: But if you want to use it against the enemy, you'll still have to take several things into consideration.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why? If we know where the place is, can't we just go storming in?

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: You mustn't forget that we're fighting against a mysterious and dangerous organization that's been in operation for decades.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: There's no telling what might be lying in wait at their headquarters. We also have no idea what kind of evidence we may be able to find inside, nor what people we may be able to capture.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: But a single visit to their headquarters would be tantamount to a formal declaration of war.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: The worst case would be that we leave empty-handed, but also open ourselves up to full retaliation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then in that case, why not work with the Fontaine authorities?

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Well, you saw one of them dissolve during Mr. Lyney's case. We have no idea just how thoroughly they may have been infiltrated.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: That's true... Seems my father really had no choice...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: But things are different now. It should be a lot easier to prove the other side's guilt now that we've connected Sinthe with the disappearances case.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You sound like you've put a lot of thought into this, Melus!

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: I am the butler, after all. I live but to serve the Boss and Demoiselle's will.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: I've always been willing to take on any kind of risk for your sake, but considering my relative lack of ability, I've spent my time keeping secrets, performing basic investigations, and waiting for the right time to come.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Thank you for all of that, Melus. Have you discovered anything new in the past few years?

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Let me think... One conclusion I came to was that the enemy must be quite familiar with Spina di Rosula, or at least, have an informant planted here.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: When I announced orders to the organization's members on Demoiselle's behalf, I used to deliberately keep a few people in the dark, and observe the reactions of the Sinthe vendors.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: If the vendors didn't change their plans, then the individuals informed of our orders must be innocent. If the vendors packed up and fled, however, then someone must have given them the news.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: After several rounds of testing and investigative tracing, I've narrowed the suspect list down to three people.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: The first is Florent, Spina di Rosula's senior adviser.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Huh? Florent?

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Yes. Surprising, isn't it? He was one of the people Boss trusted the most, which also means that he was someone who understood Boss really well.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Thanks to his position within Boss' innermost circle, he always knew our upcoming plans, and could thus avoid capture this whole time.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: There's someone else like him, too. Marcel, the head of Confrerie of Cabriere.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Uncle Marcel...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What is this "Confrerie"?

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: It's a guild in Poisson. Boss helped it to grow to its current size and prominence.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: In the beginning, they were only reselling some daily goods, but now, they're one of the richest guilds around with a lot of business connections in the city.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, they're like a sister organization of Spina di Rosula?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Yes, you can say that. When we were fighting against the Sinthe dealers, they provided us with plenty of support.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: It's a bit difficult to imagine someone using their own money to hunt down themselves...

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: The final suspect is Thierry, the man responsible for coordinating information between Spina di Rosula and the Gardes.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Although the Gardes mostly leave us to our own devices, there are still many activities we have to report to the local authorities.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Since Thierry is always in the know about our current activities, he could theoretically always plan one step ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I see... These are all people who I communicate with quite regularly.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: To think that the enemy we've been fighting against has been right next to me all along, among those I trust the most... It's almost too hard to believe...

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: If you want to investigate them, please take every precaution to not alert the quarry. Judging from our experience, the enemy is extremely cautious.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Of course, and thank you, Melus. You've provided us with a lot of great information.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: You're too kind, my lady. I'm just doing my duty.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Ah, and before I forget, proving Boss' innocence would also mean clearing him of blame in Jacques' death...

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: After that incident, Jacques' wife and daughter were taken into the Spina's care. They still live in Poisson today.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: If it might help, you could also pay them a visit. I can make the necessary arrangements.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, thank you so much, Melus! You really are the best!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: A new case awaits, my dear partner.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Leave it to me.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I hope we can work together to uncover the truth, and end this case once and for all.

talks.objective: Go to the Chief Justice's office

dialogues.speaker: Sedene
dialogues.text: Halt! Please state your business here. The Chief Justice is presently occupied with official matters.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... This place does look pretty heavily guarded. Guess that proves that Neuvillette's files are really secure!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hey, don't you recognize us?

dialogues.speaker: Sedene
dialogues.text: Huh? Who are you? Just to be clear, I don't care who you are or who you might be related to, our rules make no exceptions.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: See? They've got great discipline, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep yep, Paimon can tell!

dialogues.speaker: Sedene
dialogues.text: ...If you're just here to crack jokes, I can point you towards the exit. Unlike some, we're busy, so please leave if you don't have a reason to be here.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: No, no, what I meant to say is, shouldn't you remember us from a few days ago? We were at the trial of the Great Magician Lyney.

dialogues.speaker: Sedene
dialogues.text: Ohhhh! Yes, I remember, I read about it in The Steambird. You... You must be Lyney's attorneys. It's all coming back to me now.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: We're here today to report and archive some information on a follow-up case.

dialogues.speaker: Sedene
dialogues.text: Huh? Is that even a thing...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Of course! Don't worry, we're here on official business. You can trust us.

dialogues.speaker: Sedene
dialogues.text: Alright, then I'll let you through. The Chief Justice is just inside.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Thanks so much!

talks.objective: Go to the Chief Justice's office

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Melus, we're back!

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Apologies for the wait, Demoiselle, and our most important partners.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: You said before that you still had some business at the Court. What brings you back to Poisson so quickly?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Uh, about that... it's because my partner here reminded me of something really important. You see, what if my father's case had something to do with Water from the Primordial Sea?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: You still remember, right, Melus? On that night, it was raining...

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Yes, the case was quite similar to that of Mr. Lyney's. Both were what you'd call "impossible murders."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could the mastermind be the same person?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Could you tell us a bit more about what happened before?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Yeah, of course. Many years ago, something called "Sinthe" began to gain popularity in Poisson.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: At a glance, it was a kind of drink that could excite your mood and produce many pleasant hallucinations.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, didn't that Garde guy who turned into water also mention that the Primordial Water could be used to produce some kind of potion?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Yes, he did. Considering what we know now, it's almost certain that Sinthe is created using Water from the Primordial Sea.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: If you drink Sinthe for an extended amount of time, you'll suffer many side effects, such as losing the ability to focus or control your emotions.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: And if you were to stop drinking it completely... you'll experience flashes of paranoia and anxiety, while lacking energy to do anything. It's an extremely dangerous substance.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: As he oversaw Poisson, my father was compelled to put a stop to Sinthe abuse, and called for a complete ban of it.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Boss' uncompromising attitude incurred the Sinthe vendors' wrath, but no matter how much they threatened or bribed him, he refused to yield.

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: Not only that, Boss became determined to find the mastermind behind the Sinthe operation, and put an end to the problem once and for all.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Yes, but the enemy was very cunning, so he could never get anything out of the dealers, all of whom only sold the stuff and weren't privy to the rest of the operation.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Recognizing that, my father decided to contact the dealers in secret, and cultivate personal relationships with them. Finally, he was able to convince someone to become his informant.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: The man's name was Jacques. He felt greatly ashamed about his work after seeing many families destroyed by Sinthe abuse.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: That night, my father hosted a banquet at this countryside estate. He planned to meet up and exchange information with Jacques over some food.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: But then we heard two gunshots from the courtyard. We raced to the scene and found my father, still holding a gun, and Jacques, who was already dead on the ground...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? How did that happen? Weren't they on the same side?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Sounds just like Lyney's case, doesn't it? In both cases the culprit seemed obvious, but neither appeared to have any motive at all.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Looking back on it, though, I now believe the most important clue was something we all overlooked at the time — there were pieces of clothing left at the scene.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So they could have belonged to someone who got dissolved?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Precisely. It's all thanks to you that I made the connection now. Back then, we all just thought they were some costumes that Jacques used to disguise himself at the banquet.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: But considering it now, it's almost certain that they belonged to a third person at the scene. With one extra person, we'll also need to reconsider why the two shots were fired.

choices.text: Maybe your father got into an argument with Jacques...?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: You're right, we still don't know what happened, but my intuition tells me that we're on the right track to figuring it all out. I'm finally headed towards the truth...

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: Jacques was an empathetic man who was infinitely remorseful for his past actions. It's unlikely that he turned on Boss with zero warning.

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: I think this "third person" is probably the key to the full truth.

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: On that note, however... Even though this will not please you, Demoiselle, as your and your father's butler, I must still offer a word of warning.

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: Our opponent is insidious and cruel. They are extremely difficult to deal with, and Boss has already lost his life trying to bring them to justice.

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: Even though Spina di Rosula has lost most of its former glory, Poisson has welcomed a new time of peace, and we have been allowed to live out our lives...

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: There's no need to follow your father's path. It would be both wise and in line with Boss' wishes to step back and give up on the case.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: If that's indeed what he wished for, then he should have told me that himself.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Was I not the closest person to him? And yet, I was the one most kept in the dark.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: What was the point of him dying without sharing any of the secrets he knew? Did he manage to protect anything in the end?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Sinthe is still here, "Callas the Unfaithful" is still his epithet, and Spina di Rosula is barely getting by. Nothing has changed.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Did he think I'd just accept his meaningless death, and live out my life just as meaninglessly?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I've never accepted that, ever. Not since that day, and certainly not now.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I want to find out the real answer for everyone's sake. For the missing girls... for the victims... and for myself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Navia...

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: This is indeed the best moment to act. Your partner appears to be quite reliable, and more importantly, Demoiselle, I think you're also ready to take this on.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: So you do know something else, Melus.

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: Yes, I do. In fact, even before that banquet, Boss already knew of the connection between Sinthe and the serial disappearances case.

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: But what drove all the tensions to the boiling point was the revelation that you, Demoiselle, had been selected as the next target to "disappear."

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: What...

choices.text: But it's also possible that the third person was to blame.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Sorry to barge in, Monsieur Neuvillette. We only lied to get in because we didn't know any other way...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: It's alright. Please let me know how I may be of assistance to you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh, so you're not mad at us?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: We're looking for a man called "Vacher." He may have been an eyewitness in the serial disappearances case. If we can find him, we may be able to unearth some key information on the case.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Ah, I see. In that case, please wait here a moment while I browse through the files.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Who knew that Neuvillette would be so easy to talk to...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Unfortunately...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I'm quite certain that no one by the name of "Vacher" has been involved in any case, criminal or civil, in the past several years.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: There are no records of him either in the files or in my memory.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, what if it was really all just a dream?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Is that so... Alright then, thank you so much, Monsieur Neuvillette. We'll take our leave now.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Ahem...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: ...Miss Navia, I can understand how you feel.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Your father, Callas, was a truly exceptional man. We deeply regret his passing.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: And what are you trying to say, Monsieur Neuvillette?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Are you trying to console me? Extend your sympathy? Or just express some tendril of regret...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: No... You are not trying to do any of that. I can hear it in your voice. There's no emotion behind your words — you only said those things because you felt like you should.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: It's just like last time. After my father took his place in the Duelists' Ring, I pushed through the guards to talk to you as a last resort...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: You even told me then that you thought there was something fishy with the case, yet you still allowed the duel to go ahead.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: In your eyes, the value of a human life is nothing compared to those cold laws you hold so dear.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: If you truly regret my father's death, then why didn't you call a stop to the duel!?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Why didn't you... give me the power to stop him from throwing his life away, why did you just let him die, despised and hated by all...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Everything was hanging on a thread at that moment... Just the tiniest effort could have changed everything.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: There are still so many things I never got to tell him... So many questions he still owes me answers to...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: If you really have no heart, then just look me in the eyes — I, Navia, will show you the true meaning of "regret"!

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: ...I'm sorry, Miss Navia.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: You and my father are truly alike. You'd keep all kinds of things in your heart, and never say a word to anyone.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: It's not so much that you can't feel, but that you would never express anything.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Oh well... In any case, everyone already knows full well the apathy of the Chief Justice.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: #My apologies for taking my emotions out on you, Monsieur Chief Justice. Let's go, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

choices.text: So we're back to square one...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Navia... Are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I'm fine...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Ah... rain... It's raining.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're right... Wasn't it still sunny when we went into the building? And there shouldn't be any active trials today, how strange...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Now that I think of it... On the day my father was convicted of murder, it was also raining.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Rain...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #What is it, {NICKNAME}? Did you think of something?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Yeah, he was outside... It was uncovered and the rain could fall there. Why? Do you think the rain could have affected the crime scene?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: That thought has occurred to us before. We've even expanded the search area to try to account for that, but didn't find anything of value.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But there was something you didn't know at the time.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Oh? Wait, you don't mean...!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The fact that people can be turned into water.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you're saying that the true murderer could have been turned into water? And then got washed away with the rain...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... And if that's what had happened, then no one would have believed your dad even if he explained what he saw to the authorities!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I really think I've found a true genius for a partner... You're completely right, how did I not connect the dots earlier...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Alright, let's go to Poisson! With this new lead in mind, we'll get to the bottom of my father's case for sure!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! We're gonna make progress for sure this time!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Do you want to go with me now, or do you want to head over by yourself later?

choices.text: We should go while the idea's still fresh!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Great. Let's go, then.

choices.text: You can go first, I'll join you later.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Alright, then I'll wait for you at Poisson.

choices.text: Was he outside when it happened?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woah, what a huge ship! Why would a ship be anchored at a place like this?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hehe, there's no need to be so surprised. While it may look like a ship, it's actually Spina di Rosula's headquarters.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: My father was the one who asked for it to be built like this. Perhaps our taste in exterior design is the only thing we occasionally had in common.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: A gigantic and glamorous ship embodies discovery, opportunity, ambition, and conquest. It symbolizes Spina di Rosula's bright and limitless future.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I think I'm starting to get why you like it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And Paimon thought you were bluffing when you said Spina di Rosula had a glorious past!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon was confused why a group with such a history would live in the sewers...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But now that Paimon has seen this ship for herself, she's been convinced!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, Poisson is where Spina di Rosula began, after all. It's our main base, our home.

talks.objective: Talk to Melus on the ship

dialogues.speaker: Melus
dialogues.text: It is settled, then. Please excuse me, and enjoy your conversation at your leisure.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Thank you for arranging everything for us, Melus.

dialogues.speaker: Coralie
dialogues.text: Excuse me, Miss... Do you need anything from us?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Navia's all quiet... This isn't like her at all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's not bother her for now.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I'm sorry that I only came to visit after all this time. After what happened... I didn't know how I was supposed to face the two of you.

dialogues.speaker: Coralie
dialogues.text: Ah, if it's about that, there's no need to apologize. After my husband died, Spina di Rosula sent us a lot of Mora and support. I understood your guilt and apology to be genuine.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: But aren't all of those things nothing compared to the loss of Jacques?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I can understand the kind of pain that comes with losing a father so needlessly.

dialogues.speaker: Adele
dialogues.text: ...You don't understand at all.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I didn't know how to face you because I didn't know what I could possibly bring as a consolation gift.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I know only the full truth could bring closure to you — and to all of us.

dialogues.speaker: Adele
dialogues.text: Mhm...

dialogues.speaker: Coralie
dialogues.text: I'm sorry... I appreciate the sentiment, but you don't have to carry all that guilt.

dialogues.speaker: Coralie
dialogues.text: On the matter regarding my husband, my daughter and I have more or less found our answer already...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Would you mind sharing it with me? I really can't believe that my father could ever bring himself to shoot Jacques.

dialogues.speaker: Coralie
dialogues.text: I always knew that my husband's money was earned through others' suffering. He told me countless times that if he could turn back the clock, he would never go into the Sinthe business again.

dialogues.speaker: Coralie
dialogues.text: He had many regrets, and felt that he took the idea of providing for his family too literally. For the longest time, he thought Mora was everything.

dialogues.speaker: Coralie
dialogues.text: So when Mr. Callas came to him with a proposal, he accepted it almost immediately.

dialogues.speaker: Coralie
dialogues.text: He tried to be as careful as he could, but even so, he was still found out by the higher-ups...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: They found out about his betrayal?

dialogues.speaker: Adele
dialogues.text: Papa didn't say that exactly, but Papa did tell me that I should never be ungrateful.

dialogues.speaker: Coralie
dialogues.text: Before he left that day, he told me that he had no choice. It was only later that I realized it was his final farewell to the two of us.

response.speaker: Coralie
response.text: I don't know that for sure, but you could say that's... the conclusion I eventually came to.

response.speaker: Coralie
response.text: Which is why I'm the one who should feel guilty. Callas had always taken great care of us, both when he was still alive, and after he passed away...

response.speaker: Coralie
response.text: Even if he fired the shot that killed my husband, it was likely in self-defense. It is impossible for me to hate him for what he had done.

response.speaker: Adele
response.text: But Mama, why is Papa still the bad guy if he did the right thing?

response.speaker: Adele
response.text: Papa always wanted to be a good man, so why did he have to do a bad thing in the end?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Well, things aren't always as they seem. You still feel like your Papa was a good man, right?

response.speaker: Adele
response.text: Yeah, Papa was a really good man. The best in the whole world...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Then you should hold onto that. If a good man had to do a bad thing, then he must have had his reasons.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Regardless of whether he left you a parasol or a sword, he must have done so to give you a better life.

response.speaker: Adele
response.text: Oh...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Thank you for everything you've told me. I will definitely find the truth. The current state of things is not something I'm willing to just sit back and accept.

response.speaker: Coralie
response.text: Thank you. I'm very grateful to hear this from you.

response.speaker: Coralie
response.text: Even though your personality is quite different from your father's, your determination when you speak is really similar...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: ...You really think so?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: That's the first time anyone's said that to me.

choices.text: Someone ordered Jacques to take out Callas?

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: Greetings, Boss. How may I be of assistance today?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I'm sure you've heard about what happened at the opera house? Someone got turned into water right in front of us...

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: Yeah, I've heard... With something that dramatic, I'm sure journalists will milk it for all its worth, and it'll be all the talk for the next several weeks.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: It also reminded me... On the day that the incident happened with my father, it was raining outside, and we found some clothes left at the scene...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: After my partner here put the dots together for me, I feel like we should try to reopen his case.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Can you do me a favor and try to recall what happened that night?

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: Hmm, let me think... Mr. Callas was feeling pretty upbeat that day, so he was drinking and bantering away with us at the table.

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: After that, he told us that he wanted to go get some fresh air, so we let him go without thinking much of it. Who knew that we would hear two gunshots ring out right after...

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: My first reaction was that Mr. Callas' life was in danger, so I grabbed my holster and made a mad dash towards the scene.

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: But when I got there, it was already too late. Mr. Callas was standing over a dead body with a gun in his hands. All we could do was look back and forth at each other, not knowing what to say...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: So you also remember two gunshots, then?

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: Indeed. The Gardes said the first shot didn't hit anyone, while the second killed Jacques... but I've never really bought that explanation.

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: Reason being, Mr. Callas had left his gun on the table. I even made sure to confirm that before running to the scene.

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: But according to the Gardes, that doesn't mean he couldn't have had other guns on his person.

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: About the clothes left at the scene that you mentioned... Do you think there was a third person there who was turned into water?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's very possible.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: At least from our perspective, my father had no reason to kill, so he would also have no reason to bring an extra gun with him.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: The gun he was holding probably belonged to Jacques, or a third person on the scene.

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: Yeah, that makes a lot of sense. So you're saying... Mr. Callas ended up with the gun because he seized it from one of the other guys?

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: But hold on, if that's what had happened, then why didn't he share the truth with any of us?

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: He didn't even want to face the Oratrice Machine, and chose instead to prove his honor in a duel...

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: Did he lose all faith in the courts after seeing someone dissolve right in front of his eyes?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: About that... Melus told me a thing or two, so I think I can understand why he committed to the duel.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I'll tell you everything once the whole truth has been revealed.

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: I understand. Then, I'll leave Mr. Callas' honor in your hands, Boss.

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: And if I may just say one more thing... The whole "Callas the Unfaithful" epithet has been a thorn in my side since the day it was invented.

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: Many people have laughed at me for still calling him "Mr. Callas" even after so many years have passed.

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: But it was Mr. Callas' trust that allowed me to rise through the ranks of Spina di Rosula and live the life I lead today.

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: No matter what others might say, he'll always be the man I respect the most, and he'll always be my Boss.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I will definitely find the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: You and all our other comrades at the Spina deserve to know the truth as well.

talks.objective: Go to the Court of Fontaine and speak to Thierry

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hey, Thierry. It's me.

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: Oho, now what brings you here, Miss Navia? I've heard that you made quite the name for yourself at the opera house.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Haha, so you've caught news of that already?

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: Oh, okay... Hey, I'm also a member of the Gardes, you know. The way you make it sound, people would think I was sent off to Poisson because I had done something wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Are you sure there isn't a little bit of truth in that? Under normal circumstances, shouldn't you have been called back to the city already?

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: Haha, I mean, where I work is really up to me. Let's just say I enjoy the ambience of Poisson.

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: Callas did a fantastic job running the town, building Spina di Rosula from the ground up, and clearing many obstructions in my way.

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: It would be next to impossible for me to find a similarly easy but high-paying job in the city.

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: Anyway, enough chitchat, are these two friends of yours? You here for some formal business?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Ah yes, these two are my partners.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: What happened at the opera house made us realize that Lyney's case and my father's may be related. We're trying to re-investigate the details of my father's old case.

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: Ah, I get it. You think there might be more to the case now that we know people can be dissolved into water, right? I was also flabbergasted when I first heard of it.

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: If you want to go through the original files from your father's case, I can help you look for them.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: That'd be much appreciated, thank you. Actually, I have another question — do you have the authority to dispatch Gardemeks?

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: Of course! Without them, I couldn't possibly handle Poisson on my own.

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: Why do you ask? We definitely can't use them to forcefully get more evidence for your father's case.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, you see, just recently we were attacked by a horde of unnumbered Gardemeks in the city.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: So if you hypothetically wanted to do something against me, all you would need to do is get rid of the meka's serial numbers and send them after me...

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: Hahaha, then you think too highly of my abilities. "Dispatching" meka is very different from "controlling" them.

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: If I had to make an analogy... when you order a dish, the chef will make it for you. You can ask the chef to cook, but not to massage your shoulders, or carry your baggage.

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: If you try to make unreasonable demands, the chef would just think you're out of your mind and ignore you completely. The same goes for me and my Gardemeks.

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: Removing a serial number is also not as easy as you might think. There are a lot of complex steps to it, and it's almost impossible to keep it a secret.

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: So I can promise you — those meka were definitely private units.

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: They're certainly not cheap, so whoever their owner is must be super rich, powerful, or both. Now that you mention it, though, being in the Sinthe business would definitely be profitable enough to afford this...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Makes sense.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Haha, then you're officially in the clear, Thierry.

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: Ahaha, thank you for the vote of confidence, Navia.

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: Jokes aside, I'd like to wish you all the best with your investigation.

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: I'll be staying in the city for a little while, so just come find me if you need any support from the Gardes.

dialogues.speaker: Calcagni
dialogues.text: Hello, how may I help you?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I'm here to see Marcel. Could you please let him know? You can just say Navia is looking for him.

dialogues.speaker: Calcagni
dialogues.text: Sure, I will let him know right away.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After waiting for a while, Marcel arrives in a hurry.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Navia, hello! Sorry to keep you waiting. I'm not as young as I used to be, so my legs are giving out a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: It's alright, Uncle Marcel. There's no need to stress.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I just wanted to talk to you briefly about what happened in the opera house. I'm sure you saw everything too, right?

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Yes, I've never seen anything so strange.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you were at the opera house, too?

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: That's right, I went there with Navia to see the magic show. Who knew it would turn into a whole murder mystery...

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: I also witnessed your marvelous sleuthing work. Quite impressive.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: To beat the Hydro Archon at her own game on her home turf... I can already imagine everyone in Fontaine discussing your exploits over a few glasses of wine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon doesn't want to become the talk of drunkards...

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Hahaha, apologies, it's just how Fontaine is as a nation. Everyone loves drama and theatrics.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Uncle Marcel, you've also noticed that other thing, right? The fact that humans can dissolve in water...

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Yes, I was reminded of your father's case right away. Is that what you're investigating now?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Exactly. I still don't have much solid proof, but I can sense that the other side has already begun to act.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Oh, and what makes you say that?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: We were attacked on Erinnyes by some unnumbered Gardemeks, and there was also an attempt to get me to drink Water from the Primordial Sea.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: If not for the vigilance of my partner, I probably wouldn't even be here talking to you right now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're giving us too much credit! Wasn't it you who protected us?

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Alas, it seems things are heating up again. The peace that Callas sought so dearly will soon become a thing of the past.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: But rest assured, Navia, Poisson will always remain a safe haven for you. If you're scared, you can always return there.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: If anyone dares to lay their hands on you there, the Confrerie of Cabriere will use its funds to the last Mora to bring them to justice.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Thank you, Uncle Marcel. But I don't intend to go into hiding. I'm going to strike while the iron's hot.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Do you have any new thoughts on my father's case?

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Hmm, about that... Sorry, my age's catching up with me, so it'll take me a while to recall my memory.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: The Confrerie was responsible for that banquet, so I was out and about the whole time making sure things were running smoothly. I didn't even have the time to drink with the guests.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Then I heard the sound of a gunshot, and the rest was history.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: It's okay, no need to push yourself. We'll ask around some more, see if there are any valuable clues elsewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Sounds good. Just let me know if you ever need Mora.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: All my wealth comes from Callas' patronage and support. I'll spend however much it takes to clear his name.

talks.objective: Go over the clues with Navia

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: You know, if you think everything through, Uncle Marcel is indeed the most suspicious of them all...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Could we be missing other suspects? Melus didn't know about the people turning into water thing when he narrowed it down to these three, did he?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Melus has always been very reliable, and his judgment of others' trustworthiness has been fair and well-considered. When he laid out his case for the three, the rationale he gave me made a lot of sense as well.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: The suspect is knowledgeable about the Spina's internal affairs, has the means to dispatch meka to assassinate us, and possesses significant intellect and foresight...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Even if I don't want to believe it, I'm starting to see how things could all tie back to Uncle Marcel.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He is someone who's very close to you, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, we still have another trump card on top of all the theorizing and speculating!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Sinthe production base!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Yes... Melus did say that charging straight in there would be extremely risky, but we don't have any other options right now...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: We'd need far more solid proof before we can hope to go charging in on our enemy.

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: Navia, here you are... *panting*... I've been looking for you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Aren't you the guy from the Gardes? Did something happen?

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: Yeah, news came from Erinnyes just after you left! We've got another trial on our hands!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Wasn't that place built specifically for holding trials? What's so newsworthy about this one?

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: I know, I know, but they said the person they're putting on trial is a Fatui Harbinger called Tartaglia!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wait, Childe!?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: What? Is that someone you know?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, we know him, maybe even a little too well...

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: Well, he's been accused of being the true culprit behind the serial disappearances case. It's absurd, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Wait, how? None of our investigations have had anything to do with him.

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: That's what I thought was strange about it... So I came to tell you the news right away.

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: If the charge against him stands, then it'll be next to impossible to get the Gardes to support any of our planned investigations.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Right, because they'll think they've already found the culprit...

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: Yeah, and it'll be a lot harder then to clear Mr. Callas' name.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I understand. Well, partner, what do you think we should do? We still haven't found any conclusive evidence...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Erm...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's split up.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hmm, split up? What do you mean?

choices.text: You can go to Erinnyes, while I'll go investigate "that place."

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hahaha, just as expected of my partner!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Since this is a trial about the serial disappearances case, the culprit's attention will be focused on Erinnyes, leaving his home base wide open...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: You're right, this is our best opportunity. Alright then, let's do this. I'll stall them at the opera house and charge Marcel as the true culprit.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I won't have any chance of making that charge stick though, unless we find more evidence. It'll be up to you to make it back in time and hand the decisive evidence to me.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Leave it to me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'll help you just like you helped us in Lyney's trial!

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: Demoiselle, please allow us to accompany you.

response.speaker: Silver
response.text: I'm ready.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Melus, Silver... when did you two get here!?

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: We heard that you'll be leaving Poisson and figured that you might require our assistance.

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: It's our hope that your confidence will be bolstered with the two of us by your side.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: #Hahaha, thank you so much. Then, let's make haste for Erinnyes! Paimon, {NICKNAME}, I'll see you at the opera house!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: See you then!

choices.text: I'm confident in my combat abilities.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Ugh, who could it be...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I think...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (If we just consider the incident with the Gardemeks... only one person really fits the bill.)

dialogues.speaker: Coralie
dialogues.text: I'll leave my husband's case to you.

dialogues.speaker: Adele
dialogues.text: Thank you, Miss Spina, and Miss Spina's friend.

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: My apologies, Boss, for that last sentimental bit.

dialogues.speaker: Florent
dialogues.text: It's just... Many years have passed while I've held my tongue. It's not often that I get to share my true feelings with others.

dialogues.speaker: Thierry
dialogues.text: I'll see what I can do for you and Spina di Rosula when it comes to Garde stuff, but don't go advertising it to everyone else, haha.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Alas, why do these kinds of things happen to the kindest people...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: The place we're going is called the Palais Mermonia. The office of the Chief Justice is on the fourth floor.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: The Palais is right up ahead. Come on.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Please, come in.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you okay, Navia?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I'm fine, don't worry. Let's investigate the three suspects next.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
